# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 62 (Bu-Vb Sk62)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk62  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 62  
**Title (English, from literature):** Wearing sandals  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Upāhanāruḷha* ("Wearing sandals") is the sixty-second training rule (*sekhiya*) in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding teaching, prohibiting a monk from expounding the Dhamma to someone wearing sandals who is not sick. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali. All matches for "SK 62" in the retrieved secondary literature refer to verse 62 of the philosophical treatise *Sāṅkhyakārikā* rather than this Vinaya rule.

Parallels to this training rule are widely attested across early Buddhist monastic traditions. In the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* *Sekhiya* 62, the *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (*Sekhiya* 62), and the corresponding nuns' Vinaya texts: *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* *Sekhiya* 62, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* *Sekhiya* 62, and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*. Close parallels are also preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya collections representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda lineages.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
